# Copilot Code Review Guidelines for Baton-C

**Purpose:** Code review guidelines for pull requests to Baton-C, a hardware- and
OS-agnostic library for deterministic master/slave messaging over a single-wire
UART, used in embedded systems developed under **MISRA C:2012** (with
Amendments 1-3).

---

## 1. Scope of the library

- The library implements the Baton bus protocol: CRC-16, stream parser,
  encoder, a half-duplex link (receive ring, timeouts, echo check) and the
  master/slave node (schedule, reliable events, states, TTL).
- Message meaning and data layouts, UART drivers, threads and interrupt setup
  belong to applications, not here.
- Behavior is defined by `docs/protocol.md`. Flag any change of the wire
  format or of the delivery rules: it needs a new major version.
- The invariants N1-N22 of `.claude/skills/baton-core-change/SKILL.md` must
  hold (slot budget, stop-and-wait, sequencing of frames with content only).

## 2. Hard rules (block the PR)

- Library sources (`src/`, `inc/`, `baton.h`) include only `<stddef.h>`,
  `<stdint.h>`, `<stdbool.h>`, `<string.h>` and BATON headers.
- No dynamic memory, no RTOS calls, no driver headers, no global mutable state.
- Public symbols use the `baton_` / `BATON_` prefix; public headers keep the
  `extern "C"` guards and a Doxygen comment for every public item.
- The code compiles without warnings with
  `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion`.
- `clang-format` (repository `.clang-format`) reports no changes.
- Every behavior change comes with a GoogleTest unit test; the reference
  frames of `docs/protocol.md` keep passing and the bus simulation passes on
  100 seeds (`tests/run_seeds.sh`).
- Line and branch coverage of `src/` stays at 100 % (the `coverage` target
  fails below `BATON_COVERAGE_MIN`).
- `misra-analyze` reports 0 violations; an unavoidable one needs an entry in
  the deviation register in `docs/misra.md`.

## 3. MISRA C:2012 review focus

Run `cmake --build <build-dir> --target misra-analyze`; it fails on any
violation. A PR must not add violations without a documented deviation
(rule, location, rationale, approval) in `docs/misra.md`. The addon does not
check the directives; review those by hand (see the manual review notes in
`docs/misra.md`).

| Area | Rules | What to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Essential types | 10.1-10.8 | No implicit narrowing or signedness change; explicit casts on composite expressions |
| Expressions | 12.1, 12.2 | Explicit parentheses on mixed-precedence expressions; shift amount within type width |
| Side effects | 13.2, 13.3, 13.5 | `++`/`--` not mixed with other side effects; no side effects in `&&`/`||` right operands |
| Control flow | 14.4, 15.5, 15.6, 15.7 | Boolean controlling expressions; single point of exit; compound statements; `else` after `else if` |
| Switch | 16.1-16.7 | Well-formed `switch`, `default` present, `break` on every clause |
| Functions | 17.2, 17.7, 17.8 | No recursion; return values used or cast to `void`; parameters not modified |
| Pointers and arrays | 18.1, 18.4 | Index within bounds; no pointer arithmetic beyond array indexing |
| Preprocessor | 20.7, 20.9 | Macro parameters parenthesized; only defined identifiers in `#if` |
| Standard library | 21.3, 21.6 | No `malloc`/`free`; no stdio in library code |
| Declarations | 8.4, 8.7, 8.13 | Compatible prior declaration for external functions; `static` where possible; `const` pointers where possible |

## 4. Embedded considerations

- State lives in caller-owned structures; buffer sizes come from
  `inc/baton_config.h` and are fixed at build time.
- Document stack usage changes in `docs/configuration.md` (for example a new
  local buffer of `BATON_FRAME_MAX` bytes).
- `baton_node_process()` runs in one context; only `baton_node_rx_isr()` and
  `baton_node_tx_done_isr()` run in interrupts; send/publish from other
  contexts only through the critical-section hooks. Do not add hidden locking.
- No function may block, wait or read a clock (time comes in as `now_ms`).

## 5. Documentation

Update `README.md`, `docs/protocol.md` (wire format, slot and delivery rules),
`docs/integration.md` (UART integration) and the affected examples in
`examples/` together with any API or behavior change. Update the stack usage
table in `docs/configuration.md` when a function's frame changes.

Every user-visible change gets an entry under `[Unreleased]` in
`CHANGELOG.md`. The public API is stable within a major version (Semantic
Versioning): flag any removed or changed public symbol, struct member or
return value.
